newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - April 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - April 7.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Monday:
* Bankers Trust New York has agreed to buy stock brokerage Alex. Brown Inc for about $1.7 billion in stock.
* Microsoft said it would pay $425 million to buy WebTV Networks, a California start-up company that delivers Internet information to television sets.
* Thousands of computer operations could face serious systems glitches when 2000 comes.
* There are signs that Larry Flynt Publishing, the producer of Hustler magazine, is in trouble. Circulation is down and the skin-magazine business is less profitable.
* ING Barings will remain in Manhattan after threating to move its New York operation to Connecticut.
* European companies are making money selling powerful encryption technology around the world, helped by U.S. government rules that prevent American companies from exporting the technology.
* China is finally taking action against and arresting compact disk pirates.
* Former CBS president Howard Stringer resigned as chairman of Tele-TV and was seen negotiating a new position with Sony Corp.
* Broadcasting: Figures and methodology that indicate News Corp's Fox is taking in more advertising money than Westinghouse's CBS are the source of dispute.
* Student teams from five colleges came up with visions of how to load and play a compact disk in a minimum of 20 steps in the Rube Goldberg Machine Contest.
* An Oklahoma radio station that switched from rock music to syndicated classical programming from a Sony unit has seen sales and audience growth.
